narr: Slow-moving bands of locally training showers and thunderstorms produced extremely heavy rainfall rates and excessive totals across southern Natchitoches Parish on the morning of July 24th. The convection was associated with a weak mid-level shortwave perturbation and an associated low-level trough, while also interacting with a very moist and moderately unstable air mass that was pooling northward from the Gulf of Mexico. Precipitable water values over the region were deeply tropical in nature, with values of 2.25 to 2.5 inches, and this coupled with the level of instability and forcing promoted rainfall rates reaching 2 to 3 inches/hour with the stronger cells. Cell training with these slow-moving linearly oriented bands of convection resulted in isolated flash flooding over parts of southern Natchitoches Parish.
ev: Two bridges on Highway 490 north of Janie Gorum Road were inundated with high water.
